$ echo one > /tmp/f; echo two >> /tmp/f; cat /tmp/f
one
two
$ cat < /tmp/f
one
two
$ nosuch 2> /tmp/err; cat /tmp/err
sh: nosuch: not found
$ nosuch > /dev/null 2>&1; echo status=$?
status=127
$ echo x > /nope/dir/file
sh: can't create /nope/dir/file: nonexistent directory
[exit 1]
$ cat < /nope
sh: can't open /nope: no such file
[exit 1]
$ echo x > $EMPTY
sh: can't create : nonexistent directory
[exit 1]

// The root filesystem is read-only, even for root.
$ echo x > /etc/passwd
sh: can't create /etc/passwd: Read-only file system
[exit 1]
$ echo x > /bin/new
sh: can't create /bin/new: Read-only file system
[exit 1]
$ echo x > /var/run/ok; cat /var/run/ok
x
$ echo x > /mnt/mtd/ok; cat /mnt/mtd/ok
x
